images.after: How a content site is valued
images.title: How a sale price gets built
images.alt: Flow from revenue, minus every running cost, to net profit over a set period, multiplied by a risk-based multiple to give the sale price.
images.caption: The profit figure is arithmetic. The multiple is the buyer's judgment about risk.
images.note: 36 times monthly profit and 3 times annual profit are the same price.

items.label: Revenue
items.text: Everything the site earned over the period.

items.label: Minus every cost
items.text: Hosting, tools, writers, editors, software, paid links or ads.

items.label: Times a multiple
items.text: Set by how likely the profit is to continue after you leave.

items.label: Sale price
items.text: Check whether a multiple is quoted on monthly or annual profit.

images.title: Three ways to sell a site
images.alt: Table comparing open marketplaces, brokers or curated marketplaces, and private sales by what you get and what it costs you.
images.caption: For a first sale, I'd lean toward a broker or curated marketplace if the site qualifies.

images.after: How the sale works, step by step
images.title: From listing to handover
images.alt: Six stages of a content site sale: prepare records, value and list, take offers, due diligence, signing with escrow, then transfer and payout.
images.caption: Never hand over a domain against a promise to pay. Escrow exists for exactly this.

items.title: Prepare records
items.text: 12 months of profit and loss, proof of earnings, analytics, asset list.

items.title: Get a valuation and list
items.text: Agree an asking price with the broker or marketplace.

items.title: Take questions and offers
items.text: Buyers usually sign an NDA; an offer or LOI sets price and timeline.

items.title: Go through due diligence
items.text: The buyer verifies earnings, traffic, content ownership and backlinks.

items.title: Sign and fund escrow
items.text: A lawyer reads the asset purchase agreement; money goes to escrow.

items.title: Transfer, get paid, support
items.text: Hand over assets, escrow pays you, then help for an agreed period.
